Public Portion 
 1. Discussions on the Ban of Kratom. 
 
Minutes: 
On September 3, 2026, the Health and Human Services and Public Safety Committees, chaired 
by Councilors Brian Santaniello and Gerry Martin, met jointly to review the Commonwealth’s 
statewide ban on Kratom and its impact on Springfield. The committee received an overview of 
the ban, which took effect August 28 and applies to all forms of Kratom. City officials reported 
that they sent about 500 letters to convenience stores and bodegas informing businesses of the 
ban, and Health Department staff began educational visits to support compliance.  
 
The committee focused on enforcement, including cease-and-desist orders, store compliance, and 
coordination among the Health Department, Police Department, Code Enforcement, and Law 
Department. Officials explained that the Commonwealth advised local health departments not to 
confiscate Kratom products, creating a need to clarify available enforcement options. The Health 
Department reported that approximately 12 to 15 Springfield businesses had been identified as 
potentially selling Kratom or synthetic cannabinoid products.   
The committees agreed that additional discussion is needed with the Police and Law 
Departments regarding enforcement and potential penalties for businesses that continue selling 
Kratom. Members also discussed preparing a local ordinance to consider if the statewide ban 
expires or changes. Members proposed a follow-up meeting to review enforcement options and a 
possible local ordinance.
Meeting adjourned: 5:08 p.m.
